input.quote: Subject to the licenses and rights of reference granted under Sections 5.1 and 5.2 and, in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder, each Party shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party.
input.rationale: The ownership regime meets the preferred position from our side. Section 7.1.1 (p0427-p0428) gives each Party sole ownership of Information and inventions made by or on behalf of it (including subcontractors) under the Agreement, so AbbVie owns what it generates and pre-existing IP stays with its owner; Section 7.1.4(a) (p0432) requires each Party to secure assignments from its own personnel to itself, not to the other Party. Section 3.8.2(c) (p0327) confirms AbbVie solely owns all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling for Licensed Products in the Territory, with Harpoon obliged to execute confirmatory assignments — the functional equivalent of the "Customer retains all rights in its data" requirement, reinforced by p0104 treating that documentation as AbbVie's Confidential Information. Joint IP under 7.1.2 exists but each Party may Exploit it without consent or accounting, so it is outside the walk-away test for joint ownership. No provision assigns AbbVie IP or AbbVie data to Harpoon (searches for outbound assignment language returned nothing). Noted but not flagged: the reversion mechanics on termination (p0624 AbbVie Reversion IP licence at Harpoon's election, and p0599 transfer/destruction of AbbVie-generated data on termination) are licence/reversion constructs customary for a terminated in-licence, are royalty-bearing to AbbVie, and expressly exclude other AbbVie Patents and Know-How; the redacted carve-outs at the end of 7.1.2 cannot be assessed and should be confirmed commercially.
